newsitem.title: GERMANY: German car output slowing due to Spanish strikes.
newsitem.headline: German car output slowing due to Spanish strikes.

text.p: Germany's car production began slowly grinding to a halt Monday as critical deliveries of parts were disrupted by striking truck drivers in Spain and some companies even resorted to flying in parts by plane.

The impact of the 12-day-old strike, however, might soon wane after the Spanish government on Monday resumed negotiations with striking truck drivers and commerce and traffic were returning to normal with security forces guaranteeing free movement on the roads.

Volkswagen AG, the largest car maker in Europe, said it would suspend output of its Polo vehicle as of Tuesday in Germany and as of Wednesday in Paloma, Spain, since parts could not be delivered for "just-in-time" production methods.

Rival Adam Opel AG, part of General Motors Corp., also said it would halt production of its Astra model from Wednesday and that a component factory in Kaiserslautern, Germany, also would be affected by the strike.
Opel has already interrupted production of its Vectra model at its plant in Ruesselsheim, Germany, saying output of about 4,500 vehicles per week would be affected.
Car production by German companies in Spain also has been hit. Mercedes-Benz AG said production at both of its Spanish plants had again been hampered by the strike, forcing it to suspend production.

A Mercedes spokesman said production losses at its Vitoria plant since last Wednesday had meant that some 700 vehicles had not been built. The factory supplies the Vito transporters and a luxury version of the vehicle dubbed the V-class.
Mercedes said production was also stopped at its facility in Barcelona on Monday.

VW subsidiary Seat in Martorell, Spain, said production there came to a halt over the weekend. Decisions about production were being made on a day-to-day basis at a plant that normally manufactures some 2,000 cars.
